statement: In 28 healthy, screened adults (14 women, 14 men; mean age 35; half had used a psychedelic before) who each took LSD (100 and 200 µg as labelled, in solution), psilocybin (15 and 30 mg, in capsules of the pure drug, not mushrooms) and a dummy, one per hospital session at least 10 days apart, in random, counterbalanced order under double-blind, double-dummy conditions (study conditions), LSD compared with psilocybin made the effects last longer and raised heart rate more, while the higher psilocybin dose raised blood pressure and body temperature more; ratings of what the experience was like did not differ significantly between the higher psilocybin dose and either LSD dose on almost every scale, which in 28 people does not show that the experiences are the same (Holze et al., 2022). Length: from each person's 'any drug effect' ratings (a modelled curve, counted from and to 10% of the person's own peak), the effects lasted on average 5.6 hours (SD 2.2) after psilocybin 15 mg, 6.5 (2.4) after 30 mg, 9.3 (3.2) after LSD 100 µg and 11 (3.7) after 200 µg (both LSD doses longer than both psilocybin doses, p < 0.001); they began on average 0.4 to 0.6 hours after LSD and 0.8 hours after psilocybin, which the authors put down to LSD being a liquid and psilocybin a capsule, not to the drugs, and they say, without a formal test, that LSD's longer half-life in blood (about 4 hours, against about 2.5 for psilocin, the form psilocybin takes in the body) fully explains the longer duration. Kind: psilocybin 30 mg and either LSD dose did not differ significantly on any visual analogue scale or on any subscale of the main altered-states questionnaire (5D-ASC); LSD 200 µg was rated higher than psilocybin 30 mg only on 'ineffability' (how hard the experience was to put into words), and both LSD doses raised 'emotional excitation' on a mood scale more than psilocybin; the lower psilocybin dose gave lower peak ratings than the higher one on several scales. These are non-significant post hoc tests without equivalence margins, with most of the numbers in an online supplement that was not read, so the abstract's conclusion that the two drugs' effects do not differ beyond duration goes further than the tests can. Body: both drugs raised blood pressure, body temperature and pupil size against the dummy; psilocybin 30 mg raised blood pressure and body temperature significantly more than LSD, and both LSD doses raised heart rate more than both psilocybin doses; on the group's average curves the differences were modest (systolic pressure roughly 139 mmHg after psilocybin 30 mg against 131 to 133 after LSD and 118 to 120 on the dummy; temperature about 37.6 to 37.7 °C against 37.3 to 37.4 and about 36.7; heart rate about 76 to 82 beats a minute after LSD against about 72 after psilocybin 30 mg and 62 to 65 on the dummy; editors' reading of the figure, as the peak values are in the unread supplement). Unwanted effects: total scores on a list of complaints in the first 12 hours rose with all four active conditions against the dummy, and from 12 to 24 hours with the higher dose of each drug; within 48 hours, counted by drug, 4 people had a headache after psilocybin and 3 after LSD, 2 had low mood after each, 2 and 1 had nausea, and there was one migraine (LSD) and one nosebleed (psilocybin), with 9 flashback episodes in 5 people within 72 hours (5 after LSD, 4 after psilocybin; what was counted is not explained) and no severe adverse event. Blinding: the dummy was recognised in 96% of sessions, and although the paper says no clear distinction between LSD and psilocybin could be made, by its own percentages people named the right drug (either dose) in at least 64% of psilocybin 15 mg sessions, 86% of psilocybin 30 mg sessions, 78% of LSD 100 µg sessions and 79% of LSD 200 µg sessions (editors' calculation: correct guesses plus guesses of the other dose of the same drug), so expectation may have shaped the ratings. How strongly people felt each condition varied widely from person to person (ranges in Table 1), and nobody took a second dose, so taking more was not tested. The study did not test which amounts of the two drugs match, and this answer gives none; the authors' figures on matching amounts rest on doses this study did not give. Three printed values for LSD 100 µg are impossible: two means in Table 1 and one in the pharmacokinetics paragraph lie outside their own ranges. The volunteers had little drug experience (at most 10 lifetime uses of illicit drugs other than cannabis) and no personal or family history of major psychiatric illness, and were in a calm hospital room with an investigator; the LSD solution held about 15% less than its label (84.5 µg per 100 µg unit). Certainty: low. Status: single study.
plain: LSD or mushrooms: what's actually different? One careful lab study gave 28 healthy adults both LSD and psilocybin, the drug in magic mushrooms, each on separate hospital days along with a dummy, in random order and without telling them which. The clearest difference was length: LSD's effects lasted about 9 to 11 hours on average, psilocybin's about 6 to 7. LSD also started a little sooner, which the authors put down to it being given as a liquid. Psilocybin's higher dose raised blood pressure and body temperature a little more, while LSD raised heart rate more. Both brought complaints such as headaches, and nobody had a serious problem. Otherwise, the trips were rated alike on almost every scale. But not finding a difference in 28 people does not prove there is none, and by the study's own figures people named the right drug in most sessions, which may have shaped their ratings. The study used pure psilocybin in capsules, not mushrooms, and did not test which amounts of the two drugs match.
population: 28 healthy, screened adults (14 women, 14 men; mean age 35, range 25 to 52), recruited by word of mouth or from a pool of people interested in psychedelic trials, and paid; 14 had used a psychedelic before and 10 had never used an illicit drug other than cannabis; excluded were a personal or first-degree family history of major psychiatric disorder, interfering medicines and more than 10 lifetime uses of illicit drugs (cannabis excepted); Basel
exposure: Single oral doses of LSD base as a solution, labelled 100 and 200 µg (analysed content 84.5 µg per 100 µg unit), given double-blind and double-dummy in a calm hospital room with one investigator, in random, counterbalanced order with at least 10 days between sessions (study conditions)
comparator: Psilocybin 15 and 30 mg in capsules (analysed 4.61 mg per 5 mg capsule) and placebo, in the same people on other days
outcome: Duration and onset of self-rated effects (modelled from 'any drug effect' ratings); peak self-ratings on visual analogue scales, the 5D-ASC (primary outcome, rated at 24 hours), mystical-experience and mood scales; blood pressure, heart rate, body temperature and pupil size; complaint scores for 0 to 12 and 12 to 24 hours and adverse events within 48 to 72 hours; guesses of which drug was given
magnitude: Holze et al. (2022), 28 people. Table 1 (mean ± SD, range; psilocybin 15 mg, psilocybin 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, LSD 200 µg): effect duration 5.6 ± 2.2 (2.5–10), 6.5 ± 2.4 (3.7–12), 9.3 ± 3.2 (5.7–17) and 11 ± 3.7 (5.4–20) h, F(3,81) = 34.4, p < 0.001, both LSD doses longer than both psilocybin doses (p < 0.001); time to onset 0.8 ± 0.3, 0.8 ± 0.4, 0.6 ± 0.2 and 0.4 ± 0.2 h, F(3,81) = 12.5 (LSD 100 µg different only from psilocybin 30 mg, p < 0.05; LSD 200 µg from both, p < 0.001). Peak subjective effects: psilocybin 30 mg against either LSD dose, no significant difference on any visual analogue scale or 5D-ASC subscale; LSD 200 µg against psilocybin 30 mg different only on MEQ ineffability; both LSD doses higher than psilocybin on AMRS emotional excitation (statistics in unread Supplementary Tables S1–S4). Autonomic (direction and significance from the text; approximate peaks of the group mean curves read from Fig. 3, not the per-person maxima analysed): systolic about 139 (psilocybin 30 mg), 134 (15 mg), 131–133 (LSD) and 118–120 mmHg (placebo); diastolic about 88, 84, 80–81 and 73–74 mmHg; heart rate about 81–82 (LSD 200 µg), 76–77 (LSD 100 µg), 72 (psilocybin 30 mg), 67–68 (15 mg) and 62–65 bpm (placebo); temperature about 37.65 (psilocybin 30 mg), 37.3–37.4 (other active conditions) and 36.7 °C (placebo). Complaints: acute (0–12 h) scores raised by all four active conditions against placebo, subacute (12–24 h) by LSD 200 µg and psilocybin 30 mg (values in unread Supplementary Table S6). Events within 48 h, by drug (psilocybin, LSD): headache 4 and 3; migraine 0 and 1; nosebleed 1 and 0; low mood 2 and 2; nausea 2 and 1; nightmares 1 and 0; restlessness 1 and 1; vivid dreams 0 and 1; insomnia 1 and 0; involuntary leg movements 0 and 1; flashbacks 9 episodes in 5 people within 72 h (4 after psilocybin, 5 after LSD); no severe adverse events. Half-lives (geometric mean, range): LSD 4.3 (2.5–6.0) and 4.0 (2.3–7.1) h; psilocin 2.4 (1.7–3.1) and 2.7 (1.9–3.4) h. Blinding: placebo identified in 96% of sessions; the given condition named correctly in 64%, 57%, 57% and 61% of sessions; the right drug, either dose, in at least 64%, 86%, 78% and 79% (editors' calculation from the printed percentages).

risk_of_bias.note: Registered, randomized, counterbalanced, double-dummy crossover with all 28 analysed (card sc_holze_2022: RoB 2 some concerns). People named the right drug in most sessions (editors' calculation from the printed percentages), and every subjective outcome, including the duration, which is modelled from self-ratings, was rated by people who often knew which drug they had; sequence generation and concealment are not described; most statistics are in an unread supplement; three printed values are impossible. Blood pressure, heart rate and temperature are objective.

indirectness.note: Rated as worded: pure psilocybin in capsules and LSD in solution, single study doses, healthy screened volunteers with little drug experience in a hospital room, which the statement says. It claims nothing about mushrooms, other doses or settings, and gives no matching amounts.

imprecision.note: 28 people. The duration difference is large and its test decisive, but 'no difference in kind' rests on non-significant post hoc tests without equivalence margins, and the peak values and statistics for subjective, cardiovascular and adverse effects are in the unread supplement, so their size and spread cannot be checked.

grade.reasoning: Randomized, counterbalanced within-person comparison: starts high (METHODS 6.3). Risk of bias −1 (self-ratings under weak blinding between the two drugs, statistics held in the supplement, impossible printed values) and imprecision −1 (28 people; sameness in kind cannot be shown without equivalence testing) give low. The duration difference on its own (about 9 to 11 hours against 6 to 7, in the same people, with a decisive test and a plausible link to the half-lives) would be rated moderate, held down only by the self-rated outcome; the statement that the experiences were alike in kind would be rated low or lower, and is worded as not shown either way. Status single study: the first within-person comparison, from one laboratory. The authors' dose-equivalence figures rest on doses not given in this study and are not used; no comparison of strength is made.
